recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Further edits would duplicate existing guidance unless BRR makes a new decision to change the Ingredient modeling approach.
issue_request: FHIR-39138 was a Published FHIR-core BRR change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking whether Ingredient should be collapsed under ManufacturedItemDefinition and AdministrableProductDefinition. The approved resolution kept Ingredient as a separate resource and required Scope and Usage comments explaining why Ingredient exists as a separate resource.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 482ac65067c4308498bf89328b85ef034a16f399, 'added better introduction for FHIR-39138', which added the current rationale paragraph to source/ingredient/ingredient-introduction.xml. Jira comments from January 2023 also state that the text was added to the scope section for review.
additional_context: Ingredient is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition still links Ingredient.for to MedicinalProductDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, and ManufacturedItemDefinition, matching the product-context model. Earlier Zulip and BRR minutes show the resource-versus-backbone concern was discussed with reuse and authorization use cases, and later Jira FHIR-31877 reaffirmed that Ingredient needs to remain its own Resource when referenced, identified, and reused.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. source/ingredient/ingredient-introduction.xml already explains that Ingredient is represented as a resource instead of a backbone or datatype because some use cases require referencing the ingredient from other resources, gives authorization and multi-part tablet examples, and documents contained Ingredient as the simpler-project alternative.

related_jiras.note: Later Resolved - No Change BRR issue independently reaffirmed that Ingredient has cases where it is referenced and needs its own identifier and reuse, so it needs to be its own Resource.
